data.narrative:
Long Wall is a late-stage Defense & Security company that has raised $544M to date, founded by operators with prior experience at SpaceX and Morgan Stanley. The Defense & Security sector comprises 24 peer companies across public and private markets, including 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers such as Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Shield AI.

Given the company's late-stage maturity and capital intensity, stage-progression methodology is applicable. Using total capital raised of $544M as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for late-stage advancement, this method implies a valuation of $653M. A peer-median approach is not viable; while 24 same-sector peers exist, insufficient comparables meet narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier), and relying on all-sector medians would introduce misleading dilution.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $555M (low) to $751M (median $653M). This range reflects reasonable upside from capital deployment against late-stage risk. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory and unit economics, which are not provided, as well as the appropriateness of the 1.2x multiplier for this specific defensible-tech subsector. A multi-method synthesis would benefit from revenue or EBITDA metrics to anchor relative valuation against public comparables.
